newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hamburg oilseed mill unmoved by gene soy protest.
newsitem.headline: Hamburg oilseed mill unmoved by gene soy protest.

text.p: German oilseed processor Oelmuehle Hamburg (Oelag) will not alter crushing schedules following protests over its decision to use U.S. soybeans that may include genetically modified material, the firm said on Tuesday.

"Greenpeace today blocked the entrance of the plant and demanded declarations we would go without genetically modified beans in 1997/98 now that this year's crop has been mixed in the U.S.," Oelag chairman Arnd von Wissel said.
"They want to block U.S. sowings of genetically modified beans that way.
"But as a crusher we can only process what our customers require and there is not enough demand for non-modified products. Besides we think the new beans are safe."
Von Wissel said the firm would meet the requests of a small number of German customers for rapeseed products instead of soy.
Greenpeace says the new beans, developed by Monsanto MTC.N. to resist a widely-used weedkiller, are a risky experiment with nature and could harm human health.

A Greenpeace activist outside the plant said police had arrived to remove protestors who had chained themselves to the entrance gate for some three hours in a bid to stop trucks moving in or out of the plant.
"But we'll continue to monitor Oelag clients and put pressure on them," she said.
"We had hoped the mill would more readily respond to demands from German customers but apparently Oelag has many customers in other EU countries, Eastern Europe and overseas."
Von Wissel said, "This whole debate should be carried out by scientists and politicians, not an industrial company."
Oelag might be able to use old crop beans to meet orders in November but there was no alternative to new crop U.S. beans between December and April.
